briefs.name: Pectoral / anterior axillary repair
briefs.foundational_question: Can the pec remain chest-rooted while its humeral insertion and anterior fold move continuously with the arm?
must_move: humeral insertion side travels with upper arm
anterior axillary fold changes angle/length with arm elevation and rotation
lateral pectoral surface lengthens/shortens smoothly between chest and humerus
must_remain_rooted: central and medial pectoral mass remains chest-rooted
sternal/rib/clavicular chest wall continuity remains stable
forbidden_failures: whole lateral chest dragged with humerus
central pec balloon with lateral collapse
weights_only_acceptance: no wing membrane trench or detached slab

chest_anterior_axilla: no wing membrane trench or detached slab
clavicle_shoulder_deltoid: anterior and posterior shoulder transitions stay broad and continuous
both sides comparable for mirrored input
ribcage_abdomen_obliques_lumbar: motion distributed rather than single waist hinge
compressed side folds while lengthened side remains continuous
no knife crease or membrane stretch
upperarm_elbow: upperarm contour changes with elbow state
forearm rotation does not corkscrew upper arm
no cylindrical hinge or fixed ring crease

residual_corrective_role: refine fold depth and volume distribution; never pull the whole lateral chest

human_evidence.citation: Ultrasound imaging of the axilla (2023), PMCID PMC10175532.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Deep clinical anatomy constrains structural continuity but does not define a single exterior contour or skin fold depth.

human_evidence.citation: Sonographic localisation of lymph nodes suspicious of metastatic breast cancer to surgical axillary levels, Figure 1 photographs of the axillary base with the arm overhead and by the side, PMCID PMC11909697.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Static clinical positioning and limited subjects do not establish dynamic timing, muscle bulk or population-average fold depth.

human_evidence.citation: Parel et al. (2020), supplementary Video 1 showing a typical healthy-adult flexion and abduction measurement session, PMCID PMC7221052.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Sensors, straps and clothing obscure some skin; use motion continuity and gross contour only, cross-checked against other sources.

human_evidence.citation: Parel et al. (2020), supplementary Video 1 showing a typical healthy-adult flexion and abduction measurement session, PMCID PMC7221052.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Sensors, straps and clothing obscure some skin; use motion continuity and gross contour only, cross-checked against the clinical axilla photographs.

human_evidence.citation: Utility of the Pectoralis Major Index in the Diagnosis of Structurally Significant Pectoralis Major Tears (2015), PMCID PMC4555516.
derived_observations: Healthy anterior axillary fold/pectoral curvature is consistently visible and measurable in a standardized 90° abduction/external-rotation posture.
The healthy-control cohort supports preserving a continuous pectoral curvature into the anterior fold rather than a membrane, trench or missing lateral chest transition.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Static standardized pose and male-only cohort; does not establish dynamic timing or fold depth through the full elevation arc.

human_evidence.citation: Evaluation of the GRASP method (2021), supplementary Video 1 demonstrating shoulder abduction and internal/external rotation measurement in healthy adults, PMCID PMC8124032.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Passive clinical measurement at 45 degrees abduction is not loaded exercise; use it to reject discontinuities, not to prescribe exact muscle bulges.

human_evidence.citation: Skin Strain Analysis of the Scapular Region and Wearables Design (2021), PMCID PMC8434297.
derived_observations: Posterior scapular skin undergoes large, spatially varying strain during arm elevation rather than tracking the scapula as a rigid cover.
Strain magnitude and direction vary by elevation plane and angle, supporting angle-dependent back/shoulder drape rather than one fixed corrective shape.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Small cohort and marker-grid measurements; use for distribution/direction logic, not exact production strain magnitudes.

human_evidence.citation: Bae et al. (2024), Concurrent validity and test reliability of the deep learning markerless motion capture system during the overhead squat, PMCID PMC11603033, Supplementary Video 1.
derived_observations: The overhead squat is a whole-body coupled movement and should preserve continuous trunk-pelvis-lower-limb silhouette through descent and return.
Tight-fitting clothing permits gross segment/silhouette review but does not expose skin folds or detailed glute/groin/knee soft-tissue deformation.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Tight-fitting clothing and motion-capture markers obscure skin/muscle detail. Use only for gross silhouette, segment relationship and movement timing; do not close local surface-fold acceptance from this source.

human_evidence.citation: Experimentally measured lumbar skin strains during functional movements, PMCID PMC12483186; dense exposed-skin marker grid through uniplanar, multiplanar and sit-to-stand movements.
derived_observations: Lumbar skin deformation is large, spatially inhomogeneous and direction-dependent rather than a rigid shell over the spine.
Flexion, extension, lateral bending and rotation produce distinct skin-strain fields; a single generic waist deformation is not sufficient.
Measured sex/inter-subject differences reinforce using a plausible range rather than a single exact skin-strain target.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Marker-grid strain fields characterize skin deformation but do not alone establish abdominal/anterior torso folds or deep tissue/muscle contours.

human_evidence.citation: Database of videos of physical exercise and sedentary behaviours (VPESB), PMCID PMC11187402; male and female biceps-curl video clips.
derived_observations: Real loaded biceps-curl video provides full flexion/extension cycles and return motion with upper-arm/elbow silhouette visible.
Sportswear and camera distance limit local biceps/triceps, antecubital and posterior-elbow skin-fold conclusions.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Only two performers and sportswear at whole-body camera distance. Use for gross upper-arm/elbow silhouette/timing; exposed close elbow surface evidence is still required.

human_evidence.citation: Kuling, Brenner & Smeets (2016), Proprioceptive Localization of the Hand Changes When Skin Stretch around the Elbow Is Manipulated, PMCID PMC5073131; control experiment/figure reporting skin stretch around the elbow during flexion.
derived_observations: Skin stretch changes most near the elbow and decreases gradually toward proximal and distal arm regions.
The inside and outside surfaces exhibit spatially distributed skin response rather than one fixed crease/hinge line.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Small elbow-angle change and skin-marker distances rather than full 3D surface reconstruction; use for local stretch-gradient logic, not exact fold depth.

human_evidence.citation: StatPearls, Anatomy, Thorax, Scapula — deltoid origin from lateral clavicle/acromion/scapular spine and insertion at deltoid tuberosity.
derived_observations: The deltoid is anchored to clavicle/acromion/scapular spine and inserts on the humerus, so shoulder motion must redistribute its surface form between shoulder-girdle and humeral anchors.
A deltoid cap cannot be treated as a rigid sphere attached only to the humerus.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Anatomical attachment reference does not prescribe exact exterior contour or deformation magnitude.

must_move: neck surface follows distributed cervical motion rather than one rigid hinge

weights_only_acceptance: smooth change through intermediate and return frames

head_neck_trapezius: shoulder-girdle motion does not detach posterior neck/trap surface

residual_corrective_role: subtle trap/deltoid blend refinement only after base continuity is plausible

human_evidence.citation: The global end-ranges of neck flexion and extension do not represent the maximum rotational ranges of the cervical intervertebral joints in healthy adults, PMCID PMC8145792.
derived_observations: Cervical motion is distributed across multiple segments rather than behaving as one rigid neck hinge.
For roughly half of measured joints, maximum segmental rotation occurred before the global end-range position.
Intermediate neck frames therefore matter: endpoint-only validation can miss non-human segmental timing.
human_evidence.uncertainty: Controlled seated flexion/extension and mostly young cohort; does not directly define trapezius/skin surface form.
